name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Scientists and their key contributions to evolution

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Louis PasteurI. Created electric discharge in a closed flask at 800°C producing amino acids
B. S.L. MillerII. Demonstrated that life comes only from pre-existing life using sterilised flasks
C. Hugo de VriesIII. Proposed embryological support for evolution based on vestigial gill slits
D. Ernst HaeckelIV. Put forth the idea of mutations as large, sudden, directionless changes

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the experimental and scientific contributions
Louis Pasteur disproved the theory of spontaneous generation once and for all by demonstrating that living organisms did not arise in pre-sterilised, sealed flasks containing killed yeast, whereas organisms did appear in flasks open to air.
S.L. Miller conducted an experiment in 1953 in which he created an electric discharge in a closed glass apparatus containing methane, ammonia, hydrogen, and water vapour at 800°C, observing the synthesis of amino acids.
Hugo de Vries formulated the mutation theory of evolution based on his experimental work on the evening primrose, proposing that large, single-step, directionless changes called saltations cause speciation.
Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution, observing that vertebrate embryos develop features such as vestigial pharyngeal gill slits that are absent in adult forms.

Step 2: Connect each scientist to the respective contribution
Louis Pasteur corresponds to demonstrating that life comes only from pre-existing life using sterilised flasks.
S.L. Miller corresponds to creating electric discharge in a closed flask at 800°C producing amino acids.
Hugo de Vries corresponds to putting forth the idea of mutations as large, sudden, directionless changes.
Ernst Haeckel corresponds to proposing embryological support for evolution based on vestigial gill slits.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs Louis Pasteur with demonstrating life comes from pre-existing life, S.L. Miller with the 800°C electric discharge experiment, Hugo de Vries with the mutation theory of evolution, and Ernst Haeckel with embryological support for evolution, giving the combination A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Types of natural selection and phenotypic shifts

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Stabilising selectionI. Peak of phenotypic distribution shifts in one direction
B. Directional selectionII. Two distinct peaks form at peripheral character values
C. Disruptive selectionIII. More individuals acquire mean character value making peak higher and narrower
D. Genetic driftIV. Change in allele frequency occurring purely by chance in a population

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the nature of phenotypic selection and genetic change
Stabilising selection occurs when nature favours intermediate or mean phenotypes; as a result, more individuals acquire the mean character value, and the distribution curve's peak gets higher and narrower.
Directional selection occurs when environmental conditions favour individuals at one extreme of the phenotypic distribution, causing the peak to shift in one direction.
Disruptive selection operates when environmental pressures favour individuals at both extremes over intermediate phenotypes, causing two distinct peaks to form at peripheral character values.
Genetic drift refers to random fluctuations in allele frequencies that take place purely by chance events, especially noticeable in small populations.

Step 2: Connect each process to its characteristic outcome
Stabilising selection corresponds to more individuals acquiring the mean character value, making the peak higher and narrower.
Directional selection corresponds to the peak of phenotypic distribution shifting in one direction.
Disruptive selection corresponds to two distinct peaks forming at peripheral character values.
Genetic drift corresponds to change in allele frequency occurring purely by chance in a population.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs stabilising selection with the peak becoming higher and narrower at the mean, directional selection with the peak shifting in one direction, disruptive selection with two peaks forming at peripheral extremes, and genetic drift with chance changes in allele frequencies, giving the combination A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Human ancestors and their cranial capacities

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Homo habilisI. Cranial capacity of around 900 cc and probably ate meat
B. Homo erectusII. Cranial capacity of 1400 cc, used hides to protect body and buried their dead
C. Neanderthal manIII. First hominid with cranial capacity of 650–800 cc, did not eat meat
D. AustralopithecinesIV. Hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit, lived in East African grasslands

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review biological traits and cranial capacities of hominids
Homo habilis was the first human-like hominid fossil found, characterized by a cranial capacity between 650 and 800 cc, and evidence indicates they probably did not consume meat.
Homo erectus arose approximately 1.5 million years ago (fossils discovered in Java in 1891), possessed a larger cranial capacity of around 900 cc, and probably ate meat.
Neanderthal man lived in near east and central Asia between 100,000 and 40,000 years ago, had a cranial capacity of 1400 cc, utilized animal hides to protect their bodies, and performed ceremonial burials for their dead.
Australopithecines lived approximately 2 million years ago in East African grasslands, utilized stone weapons for hunting, but primarily had a vegetarian, fruit-based diet.

Step 2: Connect each hominid with the appropriate anatomical and cultural profile
Homo habilis corresponds to the first hominid with cranial capacity of 650–800 cc that did not eat meat.
Homo erectus corresponds to cranial capacity of around 900 cc and probably ate meat.
Neanderthal man corresponds to cranial capacity of 1400 cc, using hides to protect the body and burying their dead.
Australopithecines corresponds to hunting with stone weapons but essentially eating fruit in East African grasslands.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching aligns Homo habilis with 650–800 cc non-meat eater, Homo erectus with 900 cc meat eater, Neanderthal man with 1400 cc hide user and burying dead, and Australopithecines with stone weapon user eating fruit, producing the combination A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Anatomical structures and homologous analogous organs

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Forelimbs of Cheetah and humanI. Convergent evolution for aquatic locomotion in birds and mammals
B. Flippers of Penguins and DolphinsII. Homologous structures exhibiting divergent evolution from a common pattern
C. Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of CucurbitaIII. Analogy where root modification and stem modification perform storage
D. Sweet potato and potatoIV. Homologous plant organs arising along different directions for different needs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze homology and analogy in anatomical adaptations
Forelimbs of mammals such as Cheetah and human share an identical basic pentadactyl skeletal anatomy (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges) but perform distinct functions (running vs manipulation). This represents homology resulting from divergent evolution from a common ancestor.
Flippers of Penguins (birds) and Dolphins (mammals) are structurally distinct organs adapted to perform the same hydrodynamic locomotory function in an aquatic environment, representing analogy driven by convergent evolution.
Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita both arise as modifications of the axillary bud (same anatomical origin) but are specialized for defence and climbing support respectively, representing homology in plants.
Sweet potato is a modified adventitious root, whereas common potato is an underground modified stem. Both perform food storage despite entirely different anatomical origins, representing analogous organs.

Step 2: Connect each anatomical pair with its evolutionary categorization
Forelimbs of Cheetah and human corresponds to homologous structures exhibiting divergent evolution from a common pattern.
Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins corresponds to convergent evolution for aquatic locomotion in birds and mammals.
Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita corresponds to homologous plant organs arising along different directions for different needs.
Sweet potato and potato corresponds to analogy where root modification and stem modification perform storage.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs mammalian forelimbs with divergent homologous structures, penguin and dolphin flippers with convergent aquatic analogy, Bougainvillea thorns and Cucurbita tendrils with homologous plant organs, and sweet potato and potato with storage organ analogy, yielding the combination A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Major evolutionary events and geological timeline

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Formation of EarthI. About 2000 million years ago
B. First appearance of cellular forms of lifeII. About 4.5 billion years ago
C. Sudden disappearance of dinosaursIII. About 65 million years ago
D. Origin of universeIV. Almost 13.8 billion years ago

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the chronological timescale established in the history of life
The origin of the universe is explained by the Big Bang theory, dating the universe at nearly 13.8 billion years old.
The solar system and planet Earth condensed from cosmic gas and dust approximately 4.5 billion years ago.
The first cellular forms of life originated in an aquatic environment approximately 2000 million years ago (2 billion years ago).
Dinosaurs dominated the terrestrial landscape during the Mesozoic era and disappeared abruptly from Earth approximately 65 million years ago.

Step 2: Match each event with its corresponding temporal point
Formation of Earth corresponds to about 4.5 billion years ago.
First appearance of cellular forms of life corresponds to about 2000 million years ago.
Sudden disappearance of dinosaurs corresponds to about 65 million years ago.
Origin of universe corresponds to almost 13.8 billion years ago.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching associates the formation of Earth with 4.5 billion years ago, cellular life origin with 2000 million years ago, dinosaur extinction with 65 million years ago, and universe origin with 13.8 billion years ago, resulting in the combination A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Convergent evolution of placental and marsupial mammals

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. AnteaterI. Spotted cuscus
B. LemurII. Numbat
C. Flying squirrelIII. Tasmanian tiger cat
D. BobcatIV. Flying phalanger

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand convergent evolution between placental and marsupial mammals
When independent adaptive radiations occur in isolated geographical regions (such as placental mammals globally and marsupials within the Australian continent), organisms occupying equivalent ecological niches evolve striking phenotypic similarities.
The placental Anteater corresponds ecologically and morphologically to the marsupial Numbat (banded anteater).
The arboreal placental Lemur corresponds to the marsupial Spotted cuscus.
The gliding placental Flying squirrel corresponds to the marsupial Flying phalanger.
The predatory placental Bobcat corresponds to the marsupial Tasmanian tiger cat.

Step 2: Pair each placental mammal with its marsupial counterpart
Anteater corresponds to Numbat.
Lemur corresponds to Spotted cuscus.
Flying squirrel corresponds to Flying phalanger.
Bobcat corresponds to Tasmanian tiger cat.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs Anteater with Numbat, Lemur with Spotted cuscus, Flying squirrel with Flying phalanger, and Bobcat with Tasmanian tiger cat, providing the combination A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Factors affecting genetic equilibrium in populations

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. Gene flowI. Single-step large mutation leading to speciation as proposed by de Vries
B. Founder effectII. Constant and stable allele frequencies in a gene pool across generations
C. SaltationIII. Change in gene frequencies caused by repeated migration of population sections
D. Genetic equilibriumIV. Allele frequency change in a colonizing drifted population forming a new species

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define population genetics principles and evolutionary drivers
Gene flow occurs when sections of a population migrate repeatedly to another population, adding new alleles to the recipient population and removing them from the donor population.
Founder effect is a specialized manifestation of genetic drift where a small pioneer group drifts or migrates to a new geographic locality; the allele frequencies in this small founding colony differ drastically from the parental pool, leading to speciation.
Saltation refers to Hugo de Vries' concept of single-step, large-scale mutations that arise suddenly and act as the principal mechanism of speciation.
Genetic equilibrium describes the condition where allele and genotype frequencies within a population remain constant and fixed across generations, as articulated by the Hardy-Weinberg principle.

Step 2: Connect each evolutionary mechanism to its defining description
Gene flow corresponds to change in gene frequencies caused by repeated migration of population sections.
Founder effect corresponds to allele frequency change in a colonizing drifted population forming a new species.
Saltation corresponds to single-step large mutation leading to speciation as proposed by de Vries.
Genetic equilibrium corresponds to constant and stable allele frequencies in a gene pool across generations.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching connects gene flow with repeated migration, founder effect with drifted colonizing populations, saltation with de Vries' single-step large mutation, and genetic equilibrium with constant allele frequencies across generations, yielding the combination A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Plant evolution lineages through geological periods

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. PsilophytonI. Lineage that diverged directly into arborescent and herbaceous lycopods
B. ZosterophyllumII. Most primitive ancestral green algae stock originating in the Paleozoic era
C. Seed fernsIII. Precursor group arising from progymnosperms that gave rise to cycads and angiosperms
D. Chlorophyte ancestorsIV. Ancestral tracheophyte line that gave rise to sphenopsids, ferns, conifers, and progymnosperms

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the phylogenetic evolutionary tree of land plants
According to the geological history of plant forms, chlorophyte ancestors represent the earliest aquatic green algae lineage at the base of the plant family tree.
Zosterophyllum evolved in the Silurian/Devonian periods and directly gave rise to the lycopod lineage, including arborescent lycopods and herbaceous lycopods.
Psilophyton arose via Rhynia-type tracheophytes and served as the direct common ancestor from which sphenopsids (horsetails), ferns, ginkgos, conifers, gnetales, and progymnosperms originated.
Seed ferns emerged from progymnosperms during the Carboniferous/Permian periods and subsequently gave rise to cycads as well as the flowering plants (angiosperms: dicotyledons and monocotyledons).

Step 2: Connect each ancestral plant entity to its evolutionary role
Psilophyton corresponds to ancestral tracheophyte line that gave rise to sphenopsids, ferns, conifers, and progymnosperms.
Zosterophyllum corresponds to lineage that diverged directly into arborescent and herbaceous lycopods.
Seed ferns corresponds to precursor group arising from progymnosperms that gave rise to cycads and angiosperms.
Chlorophyte ancestors corresponds to most primitive ancestral green algae stock originating in the Paleozoic era.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs Psilophyton with the ancestral tracheophyte line yielding ferns and progymnosperms, Zosterophyllum with lycopods, Seed ferns with cycads and angiosperms, and Chlorophyte ancestors with the basal green algae stock, establishing the combination A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Evolutionary lineages of reptiles and vertebrates

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. SynapsidsI. Ancestral reptilian stock diverging into turtles, lizards, snakes, and tuataras
B. SauropsidsII. Extinct sauropsid lineage that gave rise to crocodiles and dinosaurs
C. ThecodontsIII. Ancient lobe-finned fish that evolved into the first amphibians
D. CoelacanthIV. Amniote lineage leading through pelycosaurs and therapsids to modern mammals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Track the vertebrate evolutionary tree through geological periods
Early reptiles in the Carboniferous period split into two primary amniote clades: Synapsids and Sauropsids.
Synapsids evolved into pelycosaurs, which gave rise to therapsids, and ultimately evolved into modern mammals.
Sauropsids diversified into the lines that produced modern turtles, lizards, snakes, and tuataras, as well as thecodonts.
Thecodonts diverged from sauropsids during the Permian/Triassic periods and gave rise to dinosaurs, pterosaurs, crocodiles, and birds.
Coelacanth (lobefin fish), rediscovered in 1938 off the coast of South Africa, represents the lobe-finned fish lineage that could move between water and land, forming the evolutionary bridge to the first amphibians.

Step 2: Connect each vertebrate clade to its phylogenetic trajectory
Synapsids corresponds to amniote lineage leading through pelycosaurs and therapsids to modern mammals.
Sauropsids corresponds to ancestral reptilian stock diverging into turtles, lizards, snakes, and tuataras.
Thecodonts corresponds to extinct sauropsid lineage that gave rise to crocodiles and dinosaurs.
Coelacanth corresponds to ancient lobe-finned fish that evolved into the first amphibians.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching pairs Synapsids with the mammal-producing synapsid-therapsid lineage, Sauropsids with turtles and lepidosaurs, Thecodonts with crocodile and dinosaur ancestors, and Coelacanth with the ancestor of amphibians, giving the combination A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_EVOLUTION_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Chronological events in modern human origin

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II:

List I List II
A. RamapithecusI. Emerged during the ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago in Africa
B. Modern Homo sapiensII. Initiated approximately 10,000 years ago, marking the start of settlements
C. Pre-historic cave artIII. Practiced approximately 18,000 years ago, exemplified at Bhimbetka rock shelters
D. Agricultural settlementsIV. Primate existing 15 million years ago that walked upright and was more man-like

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate temporal and developmental milestones in human evolution
Ramapithecus existed around 15 million years ago alongside Dryopithecus; Ramapithecus was distinctly more man-like and walked more upright.
Modern Homo sapiens arose in Africa and dispersed across continents during the last ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago.
Pre-historic cave art emerged around 18,000 years ago, notable examples of which survive at the Bhimbetka rock shelter in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh.
Agriculture began approximately 10,000 years ago, which catalyzed permanent human settlements, social organization, and civilizational growth.

Step 2: Connect each hominid milestone with its historical timeframe
Ramapithecus corresponds to primate existing 15 million years ago that walked upright and was more man-like.
Modern Homo sapiens corresponds to emerging during the ice age between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago in Africa.
Pre-historic cave art corresponds to being practiced approximately 18,000 years ago, exemplified at Bhimbetka rock shelters.
Agricultural settlements corresponds to being initiated approximately 10,000 years ago, marking the start of settlements.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
The correct matching aligns Ramapithecus with 15 million years ago man-like primate, modern Homo sapiens with ice age emergence between 75,000 and 10,000 years ago, cave art with 18,000 years ago, and agriculture with 10,000 years ago, producing the combination A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.
